titulo: MCP and WebMCP in one picture: server × page, who calls whom
lead: The two names look like the same thing, but they are not. MCP connects an agent to a server of yours, outside the browser, and it is stable. WebMCP lets the page itself declare tools for the agent running in the browser, and it is a draft. In this lesson you separate the two in one picture and run the feature detection that keeps the site working without the API.
objetivo: place MCP (server) and WebMCP (page) in one picture and see feature detection with fallback running.

aprende.t: MCP: the agent calls your server (revision 2026-07-28)
WebMCP: the page declares tools in the browser
Feature detection: without the API, nothing breaks
Which course in the program teaches each side

hero_alt: Industrial humanoid robot sitting in front of a monitor with a browser, with cables running to a server rack in the background.

secoes.titulo: Two paths to the same action

nos.detalhe: Claude Code, Codex, an agent in the browser. In MCP it is the client that calls the server. In WebMCP it is in the browser and calls what the open page registered.

A program of yours that exposes tools, resources, and prompts over stdio or Streamable HTTP. Current revision 2026-07-28: no session and no initialize, server/discover required. Stable. Course 1 of the program.

The page registers JavaScript functions in document.modelContext (registerTool, getTools, executeTool, toolchange event). Community Group draft from 10/16/2026, only with an origin trial or a flag. By default the tool is only visible to the page itself, to the same origin, and to agents built into the browser. Course 2.
Without the API, the same site keeps working through the form from lesson 3. The page checks whether document.modelContext exists and only then registers tools. No visitor loses anything.

secoes.legenda: MCP: the agent goes to your server. WebMCP: the open page offers tools to the browser's agent. The HTML holds up both.

secoes.sub: What changes between the two, in four questions.

texto: MCP: in a process of yours (on the agent's machine over stdio, or at an HTTP address). WebMCP: inside the open tab, in the page's JavaScript.
MCP: the client (the agent) calls the server. WebMCP: the browser's agent reads the list with getTools and runs the tool; the function that runs is the page's.

MCP: stable, revision 2026-07-28 (tutorials with SSE and initialize are from old revisions). WebMCP: a draft that has already been renamed once (from navigator to document, accepted on 05/19/2026). Lesson 5.

exemplo.texto: WebMCP: experimental as of 10/19/2026 (origin trial Chrome 149–156, Edge 150).

texto: HTML that the agent reads (lesson 3) works for both. If you have a service with an API, the MCP server is the stable step. The page with WebMCP comes in as a lab, always with detection and fallback.

secoes.sub: The only WebMCP JavaScript in this course: check whether the API exists and, without it, leave the form as it is. Registering real tools is course 2. The detectar.mjs opens the page without the API and with an empty stub (it is not the API or the polyfill), just to show the two branches.

abas.html:
sem API  · WebMCP ausente: o site segue pelo formulário, igual para todos · botão Agendar: sim
com stub · WebMCP presente: aqui a página registraria as ferramentas (curso 2 da formação) · botão Agendar: sim
saída: 0

In both branches the "Agendar" button is still there: the fallback doesn't depend on the API. With the API present, the page would register the tools; without it, the page works the same for everyone.

abas.rot: Common mistake: a page with no detection
abas.html:
sem API  · (a página não faz detecção) · botão Agendar: não
com stub · (a página não faz detecção) · botão Agendar: não
saída: 1

Running the same test on antes.html: the page does no detection at all and has no named button. WebMCP code without "modelContext" in document breaks in a browser that doesn't have the API, which today is almost every browser.

perguntas.p: Where does the tool run in an MCP server?
opcoes: In the JavaScript of the page open in the browser
Inside the AI model the agent uses
In the visitor's browser, with an origin trial
In a process of your own, over stdio or HTTP
perguntas.explica: MCP connects the agent (client) to a server of your own, outside the browser. A tool in the page's JavaScript is WebMCP.

perguntas.p: What is the WebMCP surface in the October 16, 2026 draft?
perguntas.explica: The change from navigator to document was accepted on May 19, 2026 (PR #177). Older material with navigator.modelContext is out of date.

perguntas.p: What is the "modelContext" in document detection for?
opcoes: To turn on the API in Chrome even without an origin trial
To tell the visitor to install the agent extension
To register only where the API exists
To hide the form when there is an agent
perguntas.explica: Without the API, the code doesn't run the WebMCP branch and the form stays the way in. Nothing is hidden; the fallback is the site itself.

perguntas.p: Is the detectar.mjs stub the WebMCP polyfill?
opcoes: Yes, it's the official implementation for those without the API
No: it's an empty object so you can see the other branch
Yes, it's the same object the origin trial installs
No: it's a local MCP server the kit starts
perguntas.explica: The stub doesn't register or run anything. The (unofficial) polyfill and the real API are for course 2.
